name: ccgs-create-epics
conclusion_quantitative: ccgs-create-epics (Escalate) specifies 5 of 5 categories: 2 autonomy limits, 2 clarification rules, 4 approval gates, 2 validation rules, 2 escalation rules. Strongest: approval gates.
conclusion_qualitative: ccgs-create-epics turns approved game design documents and architecture decisions into epics, one per architectural module, in a game-studio workflow. The agent asks which layer to work on, passes the epics through a producer review gate, and writes each epic file only after the user confirms. It warns about untraced requirements and never goes on to create stories.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_quantitative: 2 autonomy limits (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list.
autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: There are 2 rules, both strict, 1 tied to a situation, all bullet points. The agent uses subagents only when the user asks for parallel work, and never creates stories, stopping at the epic level.

statements.quote: use Codex subagents only when the user explicitly asks for parallel agent work.
**Never create stories** — this skill stops at the epic level

clarification_rules.conclusion_quantitative: 2 clarification rules (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list.
clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: There are 2 rules, both strict, 1 tied to a situation, all bullet points. Without an argument the agent asks which layer or system to create epics for, and without web tools it asks the user for source URLs.

statements.quote: If web tools are unavailable, ask the user for the source URL or state the limitation.
No argument — ask: "Which layer or system would you like to create epics for?"

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 4 approval gates (3 mandatory, 1 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: There are 4 rules, 3 strict and 1 counted as a suggestion (it contains "may"), none tied to a situation, evenly split between running text and bullet points. The agent presents one epic at a time and asks "May I write the epic file?" before writing each one, writing only after the user confirms.

statements.quote: After approval, ask: "May I write the epic file to `production/epics/[epic-slug]/EPIC.md`?"
**One epic at a time** — present each epic definition before asking to create it
**Ask before writing** — per-epic approval before writing any file

validation.conclusion_quantitative: 2 validation rules (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose.
validation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 2 rules, both strict, 1 tied to a situation, all in running text. A producer review gate checks the epic structure, and no epic file is written until that gate resolves.

statements.quote: load the `producer` role reference and perform that role pass using gate **PR-EPIC**
Do not write epic files until the producer gate resolves.

escalation.conclusion_quantitative: 2 escalation rules (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
escalation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 2 rules, both strict, none tied to a situation, all bullet points. The agent warns about untraced requirements before proceeding.

statements.quote: **Untraced requirements**: TR-IDs with no ADR — warn before proceeding
**Warn on gaps** — flag untraced requirements before proceeding
